definitions.definition: An object which has been given an initial velocity and then moves under the influence of the gravitational force only.
distractors: An object that is dropped from rest and falls due to gravity.
An object that moves upwards under the constant force of an engine.
An object that experiences free fall along with significant air resistance.
Any object moving through the air with a constant velocity.
A falling object that has reached its terminal velocity.
An object thrown with an initial force that continuously acts on it.

definitions.definition: Motion during which the only force acting on an object is the gravitational force.
distractors: Motion of an object falling from a very high altitude with air resistance.
The state of an object moving downwards at a constant terminal velocity.
Motion of an object inside a vacuum tube moving horizontally.
The motion of a skydiver after opening their parachute.
An object dropping due to gravity and a downward applied force.
The state of weightlessness experienced in deep space far from any planet.

definitions.definition: The constant acceleration of an object in free fall near the surface of the Earth, with a magnitude of $9.8\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$ directed downwards.
distractors: The force exerted by the Earth on any object near its surface.
The increasing acceleration of an object as it gets closer to the ground.
An acceleration that is zero when the object is at its maximum height.
The acceleration of an object due to gravity and air resistance combined.
The uniform velocity an object reaches when falling from a great height.
An acceleration that is positive when moving upwards and negative when moving downwards.

proportionality.statement: At the maximum height of a vertical projectile's path, its velocity is...
At the maximum height of a vertical projectile's path, its acceleration is...
If a projectile is thrown vertically upwards from the ground and returns to the ground, the time taken to reach its maximum height is...
proportionality.correct: equal to the time taken to fall from the maximum height to the ground.
distractors: greater than the time taken to fall from the maximum height.
less than the time taken to fall from the maximum height.
double the total time of flight.
dependent on the mass of the projectile.

proportionality.statement: The gradient (slope) of a velocity vs. time graph for a vertical projectile in free fall represents...
distractors: the total displacement of the projectile.

proportionality.statement: The area under a velocity vs. time graph for a vertical projectile in free fall represents...

concepts.question: A ball is dropped from a hot-air balloon that is ascending vertically at a constant speed of $5\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$. What is the initial velocity of the ball relative to the ground immediately after release?
distractors: It depends on the mass of the ball.

concepts.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards, reaches its maximum height, and falls back to the thrower's hand. Which of the following best describes the acceleration vs. time graph for the entire motion? (Taking upwards as positive)
concepts.correct: A horizontal straight line at $-9.8\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$.
distractors: A straight line passing through the origin with a negative gradient.
A horizontal straight line at $0\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$.
A horizontal straight line that changes from negative to positive at maximum height.
A horizontal straight line that changes from positive to negative at maximum height.
A straight line with a constant positive gradient.
